title: The Milky Way above La Silla
caption: The Milky Way over the ESO 1-metre Schmidt telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A band of the Milky Way curves over the ESO 1-metre Schmidt Telescope at La Silla Observatory.

The Milky Way appears as a band because the Sun sits inside a flat disc of stars. Looking along the plane of that disc, we see so many distant stars stacked up that their light blends into a single glowing river, interrupted in places by clouds of dust.

The observatory is on the outskirts of Chile's Atacama Desert, about 600 km north of Santiago de Chile, at an altitude of 2400 metres. That remote, high location keeps it far from light pollution, and ESO describes its night sky as one of the darkest on Earth. Those conditions are what make La Silla useful to astronomers, and they are also what let photographers capture scenes like this one.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla Observatory. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way looks brighter and richer here than it would to someone standing beside the telescope.
